text: Vietnam and China's Yunnan province boost cooperation across four connectivity pillars

General Secretary and President To Lam of Vietnam, accompanied by his spouse and a high-ranking Vietnamese delegation, arrived in Yunnan province on November 19, extending his China trip for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Week and bilateral engagements, according to the Vietnam News Agency.
Later that day in Kunming, General Secretary and President To Lam received Yunnan Provincial Party Secretary Mo Gaoyi.

During the reception, General Secretary and President To Lam congratulated Mr. Mo Gaoyi on his appointment as Yunnan Provincial Party Secretary and commended the province's socio-economic achievements as well as its important role in China's foreign policy, particularly in cooperation with Vietnam.

Both sides expressed satisfaction with the positive progress in cooperation between Vietnamese ministries, sectors, and localities and Yunnan province, noting more frequent and substantive exchanges at all levels, sustained growth momentum in trade and investment, and strengthened people-to-people ties.

Highlighting the friendship cultivated by President Ho Chi Minh and generations of Chinese and Yunnan leaders, General Secretary and President To Lam expressed hope that the visit would help elevate practical cooperation between Vietnamese localities and Yunnan in the new phase.

Outlining Vietnam's major development orientations, he affirmed that Vietnam-China relations in general, and cooperation with Yunnan in particular, hold vast potential and favorable conditions for expansion.
He proposed that both sides leverage strategic advantages and geographical proximity to create substantive breakthroughs across four connectivity pillars.
On policy connectivity, both sides should step up exchanges and contacts at all levels, promote dialogue, share experience, and make effective use of existing cooperation mechanisms.

On infrastructure connectivity, the General Secretary and President suggested accelerating the construction of a standard-gauge railway linking Yunnan with Vietnam, while pushing seamless transport infrastructure links, modern logistics, power grid connectivity, and an early smart border gate rollout to facilitate goods circulation.

On trade and investment, both sides should facilitate Vietnamese goods exports to China, particularly targeting the southwestern market, while expanding two-way investment and high-tech supply chain links.

On people-to-people exchange, he proposed enhancing cooperation in tourism, education and training, healthcare, and cultural exchange, alongside promoting cooperation in specialty agricultural products and traditional medicine.
Yunnan Provincial Party Secretary Mo Gaoyi affirmed that the Party, government, and people of Yunnan highly value comprehensive friendship and cooperation with Vietnam.

He pledged to continue effectively implementing the common perceptions reached by the top leaders of both Parties and countries, contributing to deepening the Vietnam-China Comprehensive Strategic Cooperative Partnership and building a China-Vietnam community with a shared future that carries strategic significance.

Expressing strong agreement with the four connectivity pillars proposed by General Secretary and President To Lam, Mr. Mo Gaoyi identified them as an important foundation to elevate bilateral cooperation.

He voiced hope that both sides will strengthen synchronized infrastructure links across border gates, railways, roads, and waterways, expanding connections with China's western regions, the Yangtze River Economic Belt, and the European market.

Yunnan stands ready to enhance cooperation with Vietnam in balanced trade, green energy, electricity, the digital economy, specialty agriculture, and traditional medicine, Mr. Mo Gaoyi noted, adding that the province wishes to expand cross-border tourism, develop unique tourism products, boost educational, student, and youth exchanges, and consolidate friendly relations with Vietnamese localities, especially border areas.

On the afternoon of November 19, General Secretary and President To Lam, his spouse, and the high-ranking Vietnamese delegation laid flowers and visited the former residence of President Ho Chi Minh at 89-91 Nan Huashan Street in Kunming.

Viewing artifacts, images, and documents about President Ho Chi Minh's revolutionary activities in Kunming, the General Secretary and President signed the guestbook to express his emotions and thank the Party, State, and people of China, especially Yunnan province, for preserving and restoring this valuable historical site.
